events.summary: Central Banking reported that government officials removed Reserve Bank of Fiji governor Savenaca Narube and replaced him with deputy governor Sada Reddy, hours before the Fiji dollar was devalued by 20%. The report says the new government had come to power the previous week and was led by the army. No official reason for the removal is given; the report notes Narube had recently warned about the economy and forecast a 0.3% contraction for 2009.
events.source_title: Fiji sacks Narube and devalues dollar (Central Banking)
events.quote: occupied the central bank and replaced Narube

events.summary: Diario El Mundo reported that Nicolás Martínez, president of the Banco Central de Reserva, answered a summons from a Legislative Assembly commission investigating the debt the government had taken on and how it was used during the COVID-19 pandemic, and resigned the day after appearing. Deputies asked him whether the release of banks' liquidity reserve was designed so banks could buy Treasury paper; he answered that it was an autonomous decision of the banks. The article gives no reason for his resignation.
events.source_title: Qué dijo el presidente del Banco Central de El Salvador antes de renunciar (Diario El Mundo)
events.quote: asistió el jueves pasado al llamado de una comisión de la Asamblea Legislativa

events.summary: HaitiLibre reported that the Senate's Economy and Finance commission summoned Charles Castel, governor of the Banque de la République d'Haïti, together with Ronald Baudin, Minister of Economy and Finance, to appear on Wednesday 1 June 2011. They were called to answer questions about new taxes of US$1.50 per incoming or outgoing money transfer and 5 cents per minute on incoming international calls.
events.source_title: Haiti - Economy : Ronald Baudin and Charles Castel will have to give explanation regarding taxes (HaitiLibre)
events.quote: has convened for tomorrow, Wednesday, June 1, Ronald Baudin, Minister of Economy and Finance and Charles Castel

events.summary: The Shift News reported that Edward Scicluna stepped aside from his functions as governor of the Central Bank of Malta while facing criminal charges, and that deputy governor Alexander Demarco would replace him. It reports that Scicluna had insisted he would not resign and that a Tuesday cabinet meeting appeared to have reached a compromise with him; Prime Minister Robert Abela is quoted insisting on the presumption of innocence. The article says Scicluna keeps his salary, which it puts at 138,000 euros.
events.source_title: Edward Scicluna forced to step aside (The Shift News)
events.quote: Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Malta Alexander Demarco will replace Edward Scicluna as he faces criminal charges

events.summary: The Rio Times reported that the Public Accounts Committee of the Bahamian House of Assembly, chaired by opposition leader Michael Pintard, is examining an account held at the Central Bank of The Bahamas that has been publicly described as the account of the National Investment Fund, into which the government linked about B$700 million of borrowing. The committee sent the Central Bank a formal request for records, and Pintard said correspondence with Central Bank governor John Rolle confirmed the fund's board had never met. Pintard gave this update on 13 October 2026 and the committee aimed to report by mid-November.
events.source_title: Bahamas NIF Probe: What Comes Next After 13 October (The Rio Times)
events.quote: The PAC is examining an account at the Central Bank that has been publicly described as the fund's account.

parties.party: Public Accounts Committee, House of Assembly of the Bahamas

searched_none.note: Held lead on Ara Nranyan's 20 Apr 2016 demand (armbanks.am/en/2016/04/20/97181/) checked out. Searched the Audit Chamber of Armenia's own site (armsai.am/en/reports and its published Audit Priorities 2025-2027) and in Armenian for 'Հաշվեքննիչ պալատ' plus 'Կենտրոնական բանկ'. The Audit Chamber lists no audit of the Central Bank of Armenia and does not name the bank as an audit subject or priority; the bank's accounts are audited by a private external auditor. Nothing is reported to have followed the demand, so nothing filed.

Held lead on President Faure's 31 Mar 2017 call (statehouse.gov.sc/news/3390) checked out. Searched for Ombudsman, Auditor General and Anti-Corruption Commission findings on the US$50m grant, and read nation.sc's coverage of the ACCS investigation. The Central Bank of Seychelles is named only as the point the money was transferred from, to an account at Bank of Baroda in Britain; no report examining the bank's own conduct or accounts was found. Nothing filed.

Searched the National Bank plus 'oversight hearing', 'parliamentary inquiry', the State Audit Office (Државен завод за ревизија) and the Eurostandard Banka licence revocation. Found only an opposition request, reported 21 Oct 2020 by meta.mk, that parliament hold an oversight hearing on the Eurostandard bankruptcy; no committee, date or hearing is reported, and no record that the hearing was held or the governor summoned. The State Audit Office archive holds an undated ordinary audit file on the National Bank, which is routine. Nothing filed.

Did not revisit the competition commission fine. Searched 'Bank of Namibia' with 'Auditor General', 'commission of inquiry', 'parliamentary standing committee', 'Anti-Corruption Commission' and the SME Bank collapse. In the SME Bank case the Bank of Namibia is the body acting (it took over and liquidated the bank); the only parliamentary items found are a Speaker's rejection of an opposition motion on SME Bank and routine standing-committee engagements. No state audit, inquiry or summons directed at the central bank found. Nothing filed.

Searched 'Bank of Guyana' with 'Public Accounts Committee', 'Auditor General' and 'forensic audit', and the ExxonMobil US$18m signing-bonus account. The Auditor General's 2017 probe, as reported by Stabroek News, is into the government's failure to put the bonus into the Consolidated Fund and does not mention the Bank of Guyana, its records or its officials. Nothing filed.

Searched in Spanish for 'comision investigadora' and 'Tribunal de Cuentas' with 'Banco Central del Uruguay', including the 2002 banking crisis and the Banco de Montevideo collapse. Found court rulings against commercial bank directors and the 2002 law, but no parliamentary investigative commission, interpellation or audit-office special report directed at the Banco Central. Nothing filed.

One record filed (2011 Senate summons). Also searched the Cour Superieure des Comptes for audits of the Banque de la Republique d'Haiti; its PetroCaribe reports and budget-execution reports did not yield a dated audit or inquiry into the bank itself, and the BRH's own financial-statement audits are tendered to private firms. Its verification programme 2024-2025 was left unopened.

Searched in Spanish for 'Camara de Cuentas' and congressional investigative commissions with 'Banco Central', including the 2003 Baninter collapse and the central bank's rescue. Results concern prosecutions of Baninter's own directors and a 2023 Chamber of Deputies inquiry into the Camara de Cuentas itself, not an audit or inquiry into the central bank. Nothing filed.

Searched the Cayman Islands Office of the Auditor General and the Standing Public Accounts Committee for the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority. Only routine annual financial-reporting audits and general PAC reports on them were found, which the brief excludes. Nothing filed.

Searched the Bermuda Public Accounts Committee, the Auditor General and the 2016-17 Commission of Inquiry for the Bermuda Monetary Authority. The PAC and inquiry material found concerns the airport, Port Royal, the tourism authority and COVID-19 spending, not the monetary authority. Nothing filed.

Searched in Portuguese and English for the Camara de Contas, the Anti-Corruption Commission (CAC) and National Parliament inquiries with the Banco Central de Timor-Leste. Found no audit, inquiry or summons directed at the central bank. Nothing filed.
